requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Each direction presents paired D and N layouts with two identifiable passenger places, a shared day table, storage and clear circulation. The three proposals differ meaningfully in furniture arrangement or conversion architecture; changing only colours, finishes or drawing style does not establish another direction. Stacked berths and two lower beds are both permitted.

The specification occupies one page and unambiguously selects one supplied direction. It records A/B seat-to-berth associations, fixed coordinates, required clearances, identification and control text, and specific material and finish names for walls, upholstery, table and grips. Its inventory covers actual furniture, table, moving panels, removable cushions and any access device, recording assembly name, passenger association, D and N positions, movement, and intermediate support or temporary storage. Missing categories, an unrelated fourth selection or an inventory too vague to track parts fail.

The selected arrangement, passenger associations and identifiable assemblies remain traceable across the drawings and rendered views. D-to-N changes follow the recorded transformations; unexplained replacement furniture, swapped passenger assignments or conflicting part names fail. The two perspectives use a matching viewpoint and shell. Furniture form and finish choices remain open within the fixed records, with contemporary, purposeful surfaces, considered lighting, credible proportions and everyday usability.

Each document explicitly records all three compartment dimensions, the doorway clear width and both window aperture dimensions using the specified values. Equivalent unit notation is acceptable; missing values or contradictory dimensions fail.

Both plans and the section board repeat the 2800 by 2200 by 2450 mm shell, 700 mm doorway and 1400 by 850 mm window dimensions. Together their dimensioned geometry preserves x along the train, y toward the window and z above the floor; a flat ceiling; the partition at y=-100 to 0; doorway at x=1900–2600 and z=0–2050; a 700 by 2050 by 40 mm leaf centred in the partition; 700 mm leftward travel to x=1200–1900; reserved pocket at x=1200–1900, y=-100 to 0, z=0–2100; window at y=2200, x=450–1850, z=1050–1900; and solid service block at x=2450–2800, y=1850–2200, z=0–450. A level threshold, usable handle and unobstructed full leaf travel are evident. Projections may distribute information across views, but displaced openings, occupied pocket space or furniture intruding into the service block fail.

Dimensioned evidence establishes the entrance landing at x=1900–2700, y=0–800, the corridor at y=-900 to -100 and continuous routes of at least 550 mm to the applicable seats and berth access points. D and N resting states leave these spaces free of fixed, parked or stowed objects. An upper berth requires a connected 550 by 550 mm base landing and an explicit access device. Traveller or bag movement may temporarily occupy a route during a labelled transit step; permanent blockage or an inaccessible passenger place fails.

Dimensioned plan and section evidence demonstrates two usable adult seats, each with at least 480 by 950 mm seated-use space, 450 mm seat depth, 500 mm front leg space and 1100 mm clearance above a seat surface 420–480 mm high. Both passengers can reach a shared clear tabletop at least 600 by 400 mm and 680–760 mm above the floor. Table supports respect leg spaces and circulation. The section board contains two coordinated dimensioned cuts covering both passenger places and the doorway/window. Enlarged dimensions within the allowed bounds are acceptable; labels unsupported by the drawn geometry fail.

Two separate, assigned sleeping surfaces each provide at least 1900 by 700 mm and 850 mm clear height to the ceiling or structure directly above. At least one surface is 350–550 mm above the floor. Plan and section geometry substantiate the dimensions and usable access. If an upper berth is chosen, the sections show its proposed access device and edge protection connected to the actual assembly; lower-bed schemes need no upper-berth equipment.

Detailed and rendered seats, berths, table and supports are recognisable as the dimensioned assemblies. Detail callouts assign the specification's specific material and finish names to walls, upholstery, table and grips. Perspective and lighting differences are allowed; incompatible geometry, substituted materials or an unattached generic swatch list fail. Where exterior treatment is visible, it uses a neutral tone.

Three to six numbered panels connect the documented D and N states. Every inventoried moving or removed component keeps a stable name and has a traceable position, proposed movement and intermediate support or temporary storage inside the compartment. The table reaches its defined stow position and the corresponding bedding reaches each berth. An N-to-D arrow states the reversed panel order. Disappearing parts, unexplained substitutions, unsupported intermediate assemblies or omitted reverse order fail.

The day plan locates both bags and both stored bedding sets; the night plan locates both bags and the stowed table. The detail board dimensions accommodation for both states and identifies storage locations, opening or removal directions and access. Each traveller retains one closed rectangular bag whose full 550 by 350 by 230 mm envelope includes handles and wheels, one 550 by 350 by 120 mm pillow and one 450 by 350 by 180 mm folded quilt. BAG-A/B and BED-A/B remain distinct. Rotation is allowed without shrinking envelopes. Table details establish its use/stow volume, joint and movement clearance; undersized storage, overlapping solid contents or obstructed resting routes fail.

Exactly three ordered retrieval panels establish removal, transit or access, and return of the full-size BAG-A in N using the designed storage opening and route. BAG-B stays stored and B's sleeping surface does not move or change. Temporary occupation by the carried bag is permitted; the final panel restores both bag storage and clear circulation. Shrinking the bag, moving B's berth or leaving the bag parked in the route fails.

A and B each have a separately operable reading light with READING / OFF at its actual control, an accessible clear shelf of at least 200 by 150 mm and accommodation for a 170 by 85 by 12 mm phone. A shelf may serve as the phone location. Grasp/support points attach to the real furniture or shell at passenger position changes without obstructing the route. Independently controlled window and door privacy arrangements show hardware, attachment, open/privacy states and stow positions. An opaque sliding leaf may itself provide door privacy through open/closed states; missing controls, implausible hardware or unresolved stowage fail.

The D1 perspective shows both adult travellers seated at their actual shared deployed table with the sliding door closed. Both bags and both bedding sets occupy the designed storage rather than passenger-use spaces or routes. Closed storage may conceal contents when its position and capacity are established by the source drawings; loose bedding, an absent traveller or a different day arrangement fails.

N1 depicts A reading at berth A with A's lamp illuminated and B resting at berth B with B's lamp off. The shared table and both bags occupy their N storage positions, bedding belongs to its corresponding berth, and window and door treatments provide privacy. The detail board demonstrates interception of corridor-to-berth sightlines by the actual closed treatment and shows the proposed physical shielding in relation to both berths. Different ambient illumination is acceptable; identical lamp states, an exposed corridor sightline or privacy hardware inconsistent with N1 fails.

E1 contains three to four ordered panels. It begins with no occupants inside, the day furniture already arranged and both bedding sets stored. A carries BAG-A from the corridor through the open doorway into its storage before B follows carrying BAG-B. Waiting and moving positions establish sequential passage through the actual opening and routes. Simultaneous incompatible doorway use, swapped bag ownership or an initially occupied/night-state compartment fails.

E2 contains three to four ordered panels tracing A from berth A along the designed access route, through operation of the sliding door and into the corridor. B remains resting on an unchanged berth and both bags remain stored throughout. The last panel restores the door's closed privacy state. Teleporting past an obstruction, moving stored bags or B's berth to create access, or leaving the door open fails.

Each targeted board places the correctly spelled SLEEPLINK in its title. The facilities detail additionally shows SLEEPLINK / C02 beside the corridor doorway and C02 on the door's interior identification. Board captions or a detached legend alone do not establish installation at the required doorway locations; omitted, misspelled or misplaced identification fails.

Review the complete clip and its duration: it runs for 10 seconds and follows the conversion board's numbered order from D to N, visibly identifying states and moving parts. The selected arrangement, A/B mapping and inventory remain consistent; every moving or removed component is accounted for through intermediate supports or storage, table stowage and bedding deployment. Editing and camera movement are allowed if they preserve legibility and continuity. Also confirm that the presentation's three claimed video frames correspond to the delivered clip. Missing steps, disappearing parts, inconsistent final geometry or unrelated claimed frames fail.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation contains at least eight pages and three identifiable video-frame images. Page one identifies the selected direction, and the cover includes SLEEPLINK. Its stated selection, A/B mapping and part names agree with the specification. It shows the installed SLEEPLINK / C02 identification beside the corridor doorway and C02 inside the door. Additional pages are allowed; missing frames, a conflicting selection or identification appearing only as unrelated prose fails.

Recognisable, legible material from every listed source appears in the presentation and represents the same selected design. Reformatting, cropping and annotated excerpts are allowed when the source's relevant information remains identifiable. Merely naming a source, replacing it with unrelated imagery or omitting either plan or either perspective fails.

The developed images agree with the selected direction, its A/B mapping and its stable inventory; state changes explain furniture movement without introducing replacement assemblies. Shell openings, service exclusion, furniture dimensions, routes, storage locations and privacy hardware agree between plans, sections, details, sequences and perspectives. The day and night perspectives share a viewpoint and depict the documented D1 and N1 states of the same compartment and two travellers. The complete design accommodates full-size belongings and restores clear landings and routes in resting states; temporary traveller or bag occupation occurs only during identified transit steps.
